SVRSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southwestern Weber County in northern Utah...
Southeastern Box Elder County in northern Utah...
Western Davis County in northern Utah...
Eastern Tooele County in northern Utah...

* Until 600 PM MDT.

* At 530 PM MDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 16 miles southeast of Great Salt Lake North of the
Causeway to 8 miles southeast of Delle to 13 miles west of Dugway
English Village, moving northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Grantsville, Dugway English Village, Great Salt Lake South of the
Causeway, Delle, Skull Valley, Tooele Army Depot, Dugway Proving
Ground Test Range, and Hat Island.

This includes Interstate 80 in Utah between mile markers 58 and 91.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

If on or near the Great Salt Lake, get away from the water and move
indoors or inside a vehicle. Remember, lightning can strike out to
15 miles from the parent thunderstorm. If you can hear thunder, you
are close enough to be struck by lightning. Move to safe shelter
now!  Do not be caught on the water in a thunderstorm.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with these storms, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 29 at 7:23PM EDT until July 30 at 6:00AM EDT by NWS Albany NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...A portion of east central New York, including the
following counties, Columbia, Greene and Ulster.

* WHEN...Until 600 AM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations remains ongoing. Numerous roads remain
closed due to flooding. It will take several hours for all the
water from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 721 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicates that between 5 and 9
inches of rain has fallen in the warned area. Flooding is
ongoing and expected to continue into tonight.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in
the warned area through tonight.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hudson, Catskill, Saugerties, New Baltimore, Coxsackie,
Athens, Saugerties South, Cairo, Veteran, Stuyvesant,
Germantown, Centerville, Leeds, Jefferson Heights,
Cauterskill, South Cairo, Cairo Junction, Hamburg Light,
Limestreet and Kiskatom.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...From this afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 40.0 feet, Significant flooding reaches miles from the
main channel, flooding homes in the flood plain near Three Rivers
to Lake Corpus Christi. Up to 4 feet of water is in River Creek
Acres Subdivision, flooding several homes. Kellner Camp along
County Road 336 floods, with water several feet deep surrounding
homes. Antelope Lane is flooded cutting off access to J.I. Hailey
Subdivision at Jones River bend. Water approaches the base of homes
along the river in Buckeye Knoll Subdivision, 2 miles west of
Swinny Switch.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:15 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 20.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this afternoon and continue rising to a crest of 39.5 feet early
Friday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.
